integrations.name: Drizzle
integrations.summary: Adapts Drizzle databases and caller-owned transactions.
integrations.boundary: Workhorse stays outside your Drizzle migration graph and keeps its own schema lifecycle.

integrations.name: Prisma
integrations.summary: Adapts Prisma clients and interactive transactions.
integrations.boundary: Workhorse keeps its schema lifecycle outside Prisma migrations.

integrations.name: TypeORM
integrations.summary: Adapts TypeORM data sources and transactional entity managers.
integrations.boundary: Workhorse keeps its schema lifecycle outside TypeORM migrations.

integrations.name: Kysely
integrations.summary: Adapts Kysely databases and transaction executors.
integrations.boundary: Workhorse keeps its schema lifecycle outside Kysely migrations.

integrations.name: MikroORM
integrations.summary: Enqueues through the shipped Kysely adapter inside a MikroORM PostgreSQL transaction.
integrations.boundary: A tested recipe, not a MikroORM package; only the callback-local EntityManager executor joins its transaction.

integrations.name: GORM
integrations.summary: Enqueues through a caller-owned GORM PostgreSQL transaction using the existing Go SQL executor.
integrations.boundary: A tested pgx-backed recipe, not an adapter package; GORM owns the transaction and workers run separately.

integrations.name: SQLx
integrations.summary: Enqueues through the Rust crate's optional native SQLx PostgreSQL transaction transport.
integrations.boundary: SQLx 0.8.6 enqueue only; dedicated workers retain tokio-postgres and deadpool-postgres.

integrations.name: Sequel
integrations.summary: Enqueues through the PG connection yielded by a Sequel transaction, with a tested Ruby recipe.
integrations.boundary: Native pg only; business writes must share the database, execution context and server. Workers run separately.

integrations.name: Go Bun ORM
integrations.summary: Enqueues through Go Bun's embedded database/sql transaction with native PostgreSQL bindings.
integrations.boundary: A tested pgx stdlib recipe, not a Bun package or JavaScript runtime adapter; Workhorse SQL bypasses Bun formatting and hooks.

integrations.name: sqlc (Go)
integrations.summary: Shares a pgx transaction between generated business queries and the existing Go executor.
integrations.boundary: A tested Go recipe, not an adapter package; only pinned pgx/v5 generation is exercised.

integrations.name: Go sqlx
integrations.summary: Enqueues through the underlying database/sql transaction of a Go sqlx transaction.
integrations.boundary: A tested pgx stdlib recipe, not Rust SQLx, a new adapter, or provider compatibility proof.

integrations.name: SQLAlchemy
integrations.summary: Enqueues through SQLAlchemy's enlisted synchronous or asynchronous Psycopg connection.
integrations.boundary: SQLAlchemy owns completion and pool return; its asyncpg dialect is not supported by this recipe.

integrations.name: Serverless and edge
integrations.summary: Decides where a serverless platform can enqueue and where its worker must run.
integrations.boundary: No platform hosts a worker from a request invocation, and an edge runtime may not connect at all.

integrations.name: Kubernetes
integrations.summary: Deploys schema migration, worker, and dashboard workloads with standard Kubernetes resources.
integrations.boundary: Workhorse publishes reference manifests, not a Helm chart, operator, CRD, ingress, or secret store.

integrations.name: PlanetScale PostgreSQL
integrations.summary: PlanetScale PostgreSQL is expected to work through Workhorse's existing PostgreSQL drivers.
integrations.boundary: Use direct primary connections for schema setup and workers. Through PgBouncer, enqueue inside the application's existing transaction.

integrations.name: Web frameworks
integrations.summary: Wires Workhorse into an application that already has a web framework.
integrations.boundary: Workhorse publishes no framework package, and a web process never owns a worker.

integrations.name: Active Job
integrations.summary: Runs a Rails application's Active Job jobs on Workhorse through the Ruby gem's adapter.
integrations.boundary: perform never receives a handler context, so durable execution and the other context features stay native-only.

integrations.name: Django
integrations.summary: Enqueues through Django's enlisted Psycopg connection inside an atomic business transaction.
integrations.boundary: Psycopg 3 only; Django owns the connection and workers run in separate processes. This is a tested recipe, not a Django Tasks backend.

integrations.name: PgBouncer
integrations.summary: Runs Workhorse over session- or transaction-pooled connections.
integrations.boundary: Transaction pooling keeps full queue semantics, but LISTEN wake hints and session-level locks do not survive it.

integrations.name: PgCat
integrations.summary: Runs Workhorse over session- or transaction-pooled connections.
integrations.boundary: PgCat relays a notification only with the client's next query, so LISTEN wake hints are dead in every pool mode; pools are named statically in pgcat.toml.

integrations.name: Dashboard
integrations.summary: Embeds the operator interface in a TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, or Ruby HTTP server.
integrations.boundary: The dashboard reads PostgreSQL through the versioned dashboard contract and owns no authorization of its own.
